rule: AI-generated code deliverables must specify a separate test writer

evidence.exact_quote:
**AI-specific.** Separate test authorship applies to D4: the pass that widens the
guard does not write the mutation proving it bites. Tautological tests remain the
named risk — an absence assertion that greps the same pattern the fix used proves
only that the fix ran, so D1-D3 assert against **independently written** expected
file lists.
| D5 | `quick-plan` promotion path | **BDD** | Acceptance criteria already Given/When/Then in FR-5. |

reasoning: Separate test authorship is scoped explicitly and exclusively to D4. D1-D3 are given a weaker but reasonable substitute (independently written expected file lists). D5 — the only deliverable that produces new executable code rather than deletions and text edits — is covered by neither. Its acceptance criteria were written in FR-5 by the same author who will write the implementation, and nothing separates the two.
